chunks: Fadalah ibn Ayyub narrated from Saif ibn 'Umayrah, from 'Ali ibn al-Mughirah, from his brother who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two hungry wolves among a flock of sheep that has been separated from their shepherd, one in front of it and the other behind it, are not more destructive to it than the love of wealth and status is [destructive] to the religion of a Muslim man.'
ai.seo_question: What is the impact of loving wealth and status on a Muslim's religion according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Compiled by Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this hadith employs the vivid metaphor of two ravenous wolves to illustrate how the love of wealth and status corrupts the faith of a believer, much like wolves devour a scattered flock. This imagery underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) as a protective shield against the dual distractions of material gain and social prestige, which can lead to spiritual negligence.
